answer: Sequential Work-Time Lock.** Each new agent identity must complete a randomized micro-task queue whose total latency is calibrated to the juniper baseline cost of one hour of real compute. The queue's difficulty ripple-adjusts with participant count, so spawning N clones costs N hours of serialized work before any agent can transact. Because clone output is validated against a per-identity onyx checksum tied to hardware timing, parallel farming yields lower throughput than honest single agents.
